About us

Kia Ora, Our city is one of a kind and it only keeps getting better! We’re involved in everything, from roads, transport, community initiatives and civil services, to business, investment, recreation, and policy. We’re here to help it all run smoothly while keeping our community informed. Our LinkedIn page is used to give overviews of what we are doing and what content you can expect to see on our channels before it comes out. You can think of it as a look behind the scenes! While we welcome messages, comments, and questions on this page, please keep in mind this is a safe space and any harmful content will be hidden or removed. This includes misinformation, swearing, hate speech or spam.

    Here's what you told us in our recent local reform survey. 📢 A total of 455 people shared their feedback. Here's what we heard: 🗣️ 82.4% supported Upper Hutt being part of the conversation through the Government's "Head Start" process, rather than waiting to be told what happens. 🤔 When it came to council amalgamation itself, most people wanted a cautious approach. Nearly half (49.8%) said they'd only support changes if they clearly improved outcomes for Upper Hutt. 🙅♀️ And 33.5% percent did not support combining councils under any circumstances The strongest messages from the community were clear: keep rates affordable, protect local representation, preserve Upper Hutt's identity, and make sure residents are kept informed every step of the way. Council will use this feedback to help shape discussions with other councils. No decisions have been made on amalgamation, and there will be more opportunities for the community to have their say if proposals move forward. Find out more here 👇 https://lnkd.in/eue2JMmD

    Want to have a say on how we vote? We're beginning a Representation Review, which is something we’re required to do every six years. While there are wider conversations happening around local government reform, we still need to make some important decisions for Upper Hutt by September. We're asking for your thoughts on: ✅ Which voting system you'd prefer for the 2028 and 2031 local elections (First Past the Post or Single Transferable Vote - Check out the video below) ✅ Whether Upper Hutt should establish a Māori ward for the 2028 and 2031 elections ✅ The geographical areas you feel connected to and that best represent your interests ✅ Whether Upper Hutt should use wards, at-large representation, or a mix of both in future elections Your feedback will help inform Council's decisions and ensure the voices of our community are heard. The decisions made on voting systems and Māori wards will apply to the 2028 and 2031 local elections. Take a few minutes to have your say by 29 July and help shape how Upper Hutt is represented in the future. 👇 https://lnkd.in/e996VT3A Big thank you to Hamilton City Council for the video 🧡

    Thank you to everyone who took part in consultation on Upper Hutt's Draft Integrated Transport Strategy in May. 📆 You all shared a wide range of views on the future of transport in our city, including road safety, congestion, accessibility, public transport, walking and cycling, and how our transport network can support future growth. The feedback shows there is strong interest in getting transport right, but also differing opinions on the best way forward. That feedback is now being carefully reviewed and will be used to refine the strategy before it is presented to Council later this year. Consultation is an important part of the process. The final strategy has not yet been adopted, and your feedback will help inform the decisions still to be made. You can read more here 👇 https://lnkd.in/eZAHzc74

    Got an idea to reduce waste in Upper Hutt? ♻️💡 A new Waste Minimisation Grant is here to help you make a difference to our city! We’re especially keen to support projects that: 🔧 Focus on reuse, repair, or redesign 🌱 Reduce organic waste 🏗 Cut down on construction & demolition waste There’ll be two funding rounds available: 💰 Under $7K – open to everyone (community groups, schools, events, businesses) 💰 Over $7K – open to businesses and legal entities This grant is financed through the national waste disposal levy. Whether it’s a small community initiative or a bigger project with long-term impact, this is your opportunity to make a difference. Apply here 👇 https://lnkd.in/enCrm2Va

    This Throwback Thursday we're celebrating the 60th anniversary of Upper Hutt City Status 🎂 🎉  On the 28th of May 1966, after a week of events and a large procession down Main Street, Governor-General Sir Bernard Fergusson officially proclaimed Upper Hutt a city in front of an enthusiastic crowd of thousands at Maidstone Park. Here is some film footage of the announcement! The whole film is available to view on our community archive website, Mahara 👇  https://lnkd.in/eqUNtYSf
